observation.description: A sessions-mode server happily serves auth:'public' queries to an anonymous request that carries only the `x-snapback-auth-client-protocol: 1` offer header — but the packaged SnapbackClient cannot be constructed to make that request outside a browser: `new SnapbackClient(url)` sends no offer (server refuses SNAPBACK_AUTH_PROFILE_CLIENT_UNSUPPORTED), and `new SnapbackClient(url, {authClientProtocol: 1})` without a bearer throws 'authClientProtocol v1 requires browser, agent, or explicit external-bearer custody'. The public event preview — the anonymous Partiful page, the first surface an event app ships — is therefore unreachable from any node/headless consumer without hand-rolled fetch calls. The arm's suite and any SSR/prerender path must bypass the client.

competitorOutcome.description: Convex and Supabase clients query public data anonymously from node with the same client used in the browser (public functions / anon key), no custody ceremony. Longitudinal repeat: the 0102-epoch Snapback Partiful arm hit exactly this ('a plain SnapbackClient was refused... the arm needed a raw HTTP helper carrying the protocol offer without caller auth') and filed a guide-gap; the paved path still does not exist on 0.1.7.
competitorOutcome.reference: diaries/0030-partiful-backend-bakeoff.diary.md (Snapback arm 'What felt bad'; public preview legs)

mustNotRegress: The custody rule that protocol-offering AUTHENTICATED clients outside a browser must hold explicit external-bearer custody; uniform refusal of offerless requests.
smallestCoherentFix: An explicit anonymous custody mode on the packaged client (e.g. custody:'anonymous-public') that sends the protocol offer with no credential and is accepted only for public-auth operations, documented beside the public-query declaration.
acceptanceWitness: From node, a packaged client constructed in the anonymous mode reads an auth:'public' query on a sessions server and is refused on any protected operation; the browser path is unchanged.
